nodes.body:
`high` `correctness`

This is a 1300+ line bundled artifact committed in the PR. The same module is also concatenated into `dist/index.js`. These should be regenerated by the CI build (`pnpm build`/`tsc`) rather than committed — every subsequent review becomes a multi-thousand-line artifact diff that obscures the real source changes (`src/cli/live-shared.ts`, `src/render/summary-layouts.ts`, etc.). Add `dist/**` to `.gitignore` (or rely on a `.npmignore` / release-only flow) and drop these files from this PR.

`low` `correctness`

Docstring typo: `<!-- umalready-pr-review:manifest {...} -->` should be `umalready` → `umactually`. Anyone grepping the codebase for the marker will miss this reference. Also appears in the JSDoc block for `buildReviewBody` in the same file.

`medium` `correctness`

`buildReviewBody` now passes `postedComments` (the post-filter set) into the layout, but the layout uses `data.severityCounts` directly to render the severity tally — and that field is whatever the caller computed. If the caller computes `severityCounts` from the raw `review.comments` but passes `postedComments` as a filtered subset, the rendered `🏷️ \`2\` critical · …` tally will be inconsistent with the findings table (which lists the post-filter set). The old builder derived the tally from the same source as the preview. Either (a) recompute `severityCounts` inside the layout from `postedComments`, or (b) document that callers must pass `severityCounts` derived from `postedComments`.

`high` `correctness`

The 'CLARITY-19 pipeline summary structural invariant' test file no longer tests the structural invariant. `filtered` is hard-coded to `0` in `counts()`, and there's no assertion that `total === posted + off-diff + filtered` (because `filtered` is now invisible in the body and not in the manifest either). The contract the test is supposed to pin has been broken by the cutover — either restore it (e.g. by having the layout surface a `filtered` count in the manifest) or rename the test to match what it's actually checking.

`medium` `correctness`

The old `CLARITY-14g` test asserting `🧹 Filtered preview (showing N of M candidates)` is gone, but the layout still has to handle the `validCommentCount === 0 && review.comments.length > 0` case (pre-filter candidates displayed in the body). The new test exercises `postedComments: []` only — never the case where post-filter is empty but the model produced N candidates. Add a test that pins the rendering of the 'all findings filtered, model returned N' case in the severity-table layout.

`medium` `performance`

The second pass builds `result` via `result += char` followed by `result = result.slice(0, -1) + escape` for each control char inside a string. For a 65k-char payload with hundreds of embedded newlines (the SSE delta case), each slice-and-rebuild is O(n), giving O(n²) total work. Push to an array and `join` once at the end, or build into an array of `string | string[]` segments — same output, O(n).

`low` `correctness`

`statMtime` returns `readFileSync(p).atimeMs` (the atime, access time) but the function and variable are named `mtime`. The staleness check `srcMtime <= outMtime` works by coincidence because both calls fetch atime. Files accessed via tooling without mtime updates will trigger spurious rebuilds. Either rename the function to `statAtime` or switch to `statSync(p).mtimeMs`.

`low` `style`

Missing trailing newline (`\ No newline at end of file` in diff). Same for `src/render/summary-layouts.ts`, all three `scripts/*.mjs`, both new test files, and the modified `test/unit/preview-parent-card.test.ts` and `test/unit/pipeline-summary-invariant.test.ts`. The rest of the repo uses final newlines consistently — match the convention.

`low` `style`

`severityRank` is imported but no longer called directly in this file (the legacy `topConcernsBlock` that used it is gone). The layout module imports it from the same util. Drop the unused import here.

`low` `style`

Script has no trailing newline. Also: this script hard-codes `npx.cmd`/`npx` invocation and shell-arg-quoting patterns that drift from the project's actual `package.json` scripts. Consider a `package.json` script (`"render:evidence": "…"`) so the script stays in sync with the rest of the build pipeline.

`low` `style`

`.layout-viewer-build/` is added but the viewer scripts are dev-only tooling. A `.gitignore` entry for a single script's build dir is fine, but the pattern is overly specific — consider a broader `*.tsbuildinfo` / `build/` ignore so the next script doesn't need a new line.

`high` `build`

Committed `dist/cli.js` and `dist/index.js` are regenerated bundles (~1400 new lines each). These are build artifacts and should not be reviewed or committed alongside source changes — the source TypeScript is the contract. Confirm the repo's release process actually requires dist files in git; if not, drop them from this PR.

`medium` `build`

Even if dist is intentionally committed, the bundle has ~2800 lines of duplicated layout code across `cli.js` and `index.js`. This is the kind of artifact that goes stale. If you must ship dist, add a CI check that `dist/` is regenerated whenever `src/` changes.

`high` `correctness`

`statMtime` uses `readFileSync(...).atimeMs` which is the *access* time, not *modification* time. The variable name and the staleness check semantics don't match. This is a wrong-implementation bug — the staleness check will not detect changes. Use `statSync(p).mtimeMs` instead.

`medium` `docs`

References `scripts/clean-viewer.mjs` in the file header comment but the file is not in the diff. Either add it to this PR or remove the reference; otherwise `node scripts/clean-viewer.mjs` will fail with ENOENT.

`low` `code-quality`

`severityRank` is still imported but no longer used in this file after the delegation to `renderSummary`. The import is now dead code and should be removed.

`low` `code-quality`

`SEVERITY_ORDER` import removed (good — no longer used here), but the `countBySeverityUtil`/`countBySeverity` re-export is now used only as a re-export shim. If nothing in `live-shared.ts` body uses it, the file should import only what it consumes and let external callers import from `util/severity.js` directly. Otherwise this becomes a hidden coupling.

`medium` `maintainability`

`layoutBaseline` is a near-byte-identical copy of the deleted `buildReviewBody` assembly logic. This is intentional for the viewer comparison, but it now duplicates the same helpers (verdict badge, pipeline summary, severity tally, off-diff block, summary handling) that the new 20 layouts also use. Any future change to those helpers has to be kept in sync with the baseline copy. Consider extracting the baseline into a shared composition function so it cannot drift from the new helpers.

`medium` `docs`

The header comment says "`LAYOUT_DEFAULT`" is byte-identical to the existing buildReviewBody, but `LAYOUT_DEFAULT` is not actually exported — the default is hard-coded to `"severity-table"` in `src/cli/live-shared.ts:255`. Either export `LAYOUT_DEFAULT = "severity-table"` (or `LAYOUT_DEFAULT = "baseline"` if you want the byte-identical behavior to be the default) so the contract in the doc matches the code.

`medium` `docs`

The header comment claims "`LAYOUT_DEFAULT` is byte-identical to the existing `buildReviewBody` output so all existing tests continue to pass without modification" — but the diff shows ~5 test files heavily modified to match the new output. The doc is misleading; either remove that line or pin the default to the baseline so the doc becomes true.

`high` `correctness`

Azure DevOps comment-rendering note: "DO NOT use `<details>`/`<summary>` for short content — Azure DevOps PR comments render them as raw text. EXCEPTION: when the model emits a verbose summary (>500 chars), the severity-table layout wraps the summary in `<details>`… Azure DevOps will show the raw `<details>` HTML in that case — a trade-off we accept". The previous contract was to NEVER use `<details>` for Azure compatibility. This change knowingly regresses Azure rendering for long summaries. For Azure-only or Azure-primary orgs (the comment acknowledges this), the body now contains a wall of visible HTML. Flag this to reviewers as a deliberate contract change, not a bug — the CLARITY-4 test was rewritten to assert the regression, not the original guarantee.

`low` `correctness`

Manifest schema is `MANIFEST_SCHEMA` from `../util/marker.js` but the manifest JSON.stringify spreads `...data.severityCounts` — this strips the `severityCounts` field's type from `Readonly<Record<string, number>>`. The output is fine, but if `MANIFEST_SCHEMA` is a versioned constant, the spread is a soft contract violation (additive fields could leak across versions). Consider explicit field copy.

`low` `code-quality`

`layoutProsCons` computes `lowCount` and `highCount` but only uses them in the `if (lowCount + highCount > 0)` guard. The branch renders a section labeled `### 📊 Tally` that re-uses `severityTally(data)`, which already self-hides when total=0. The `lowCount + highCount > 0` guard is therefore dead — it gates a section that re-checks the same condition. Either use the guard meaningfully or delete it.

`low` `docs`

`layoutTerminal` only emits `c.path:line` (no body) — the test for body redaction exempts it. This is correct, but if `data.secrets` ever contains a secret that overlaps a path, it would be silently unredacted. Document the exemption in the layout comment so future contributors know.

`medium` `design`

`buildReviewBody` now hard-codes `"severity-table"` as the layout choice. The whole point of the 20-layout system (per the file header) is that callers can pick a layout. Hard-coding one defeats the purpose. Expose a config option (env var, CLI flag, or second argument) so the choice isn't buried in a constant.

`low` `correctness`

`postedComments: input.postedComments ?? input.review.comments` is a compat shim. The comment justifies it for older fixtures, but the new `summary-layouts.ts` types `postedComments` as required (not optional). If the runtime shim is needed, the type should also be `postedComments?: ...` with the shim applied inside the layout module. Pushing the fallback into the new module means a future caller cannot accidentally pass undefined.

`high` `correctness`

CLARITY-2 test was rewritten from "severity counts line is within 200 chars of the verdict badge" to "severity tally is present in the body (after the findings table)". The original contract is a deliberate scannability guarantee (severity above the fold). The new contract allows severity to be anywhere after verdict, which means a 50-row findings table can push the tally deep below the fold. This is a regression in scannability that the new test no longer catches. Either keep the original guarantee and reduce the table, or document the contract change explicitly.

`medium` `correctness`

CLARITY-13 test was rewritten to assert that the off-diff count lives ONLY in the manifest. The original test asserted that the body's `📍 Off-diff (N not posted)` block listed every suppressed finding — so a human reviewer could see what was dropped. The new contract hides this entirely. For a reviewer who wants to know "what off-diff things were considered but not posted", the answer now requires reading the manifest JSON. Flag this as a deliberate contract change.

`high` `correctness`

CLARITY-4 test was rewritten from "long summary prose is wrapped in a <details> block" to "summary prose appears in the body as a Summary section (no <details> wrapper)". The new test then asserts `body.not.toContain("<details>")` — which contradicts the new layout's own S5b test in `summary-layouts.test.ts:380` that DOES emit `<details>` for verbose summaries. These two test files are now in conflict depending on which fixture you use. Either pick one (always wrap / never wrap) and document the threshold, or have the test exercise both regimes.

`medium` `correctness`

CLARITY-5b test asserts `body.toContain("not actually JSON")` for the parse-fail fallback, but the new layout surfaces the raw provider text inline under `### 📝 Summary`. Long raw provider dumps will now dominate the parse-fail card on both GitHub and Azure. The original `<details>`-wrapped fallback kept long content collapsed. This is a regression for parse-fail scannability on long raw responses.

`medium` `correctness`

The `counts()` helper returns `filtered: 0` with a comment that says "severity-table layout does not surface filtered explicitly". This means the structural invariant `total === posted + off-diff + filtered` is no longer testable from the body. The manifest doesn't carry `filteredCount`. The test silently drops the assertion. Either add `filteredCount` to the manifest schema or add a separate test that exercises the filter calculation via a different code path.

`medium` `testing`

SSE event-grouping refactor: blank-line event boundary detection is correct per the SSE spec, but the new logic joins multiple `data:` lines with `\n` — this can produce JSON content where a single string field has a literal `\n` inside it. That case is then fixed by the new `extractFirstBalancedObject` escape logic. The two changes are coupled and untested in isolation. Add a focused test for `tryExtractSse` with multi-line `data:` events (the new `json-extract-robustness.test.ts` only exercises `extractTextPayload`, not the SSE parser directly).

`low` `performance`

The new control-char escape pass is in a second loop after finding the end index. This is correct but it's O(2N) when the first pass already knew `inString`/`escape` state. Consider tracking the output buffer in the first pass. Not a bug, just a perf nit for large JSON objects.

`low` `testing`

The escape logic only handles control chars that appear *inside* a string. What about backslash-encoded control chars the user might have actually wanted? E.g. an intentional `\n` in a JSON string value (as a literal backslash-n pair) would be re-escaped if it somehow got de-escaped upstream. The doc comment handles this correctly (only literal control chars, not `\n` escape sequences), but a unit test pinning "`\\n` in a string value is preserved" would prevent a future refactor from breaking this.

`medium` `design`

`layoutSeverityTable` is the only layout that emits `<details>` (for verbose summary). This is the layout wired as default in `buildReviewBody`. So in production: short-summary reviews render inline, long-summary reviews emit `<details>` that Azure DevOps shows as raw HTML. This is the single most-likely-to-be-surprising behavior of the new default. Consider whether the default should be a layout that's never used `<details>`, or whether the threshold for "verbose" should be much higher than 500 chars (e.g. 5000).

`high` `correctness`

`LAYOUTS` is declared `readonly LayoutId[]`, but the CLARITY-* docstring inside `buildReviewBody` still claims the marker comment is `<!-- umalready-pr-review:manifest {…} -->` (typo `umalready`). The actual emitted marker string is `<!-- umactually-pr-review:manifest` (per `manifest()` implementation). The doc comment is now stale and misleading — fix to `umactually-pr-review:manifest`.

`high` `correctness`

Module header says `<details>`/`<summary>` render on BOTH GitHub and Azure DevOps and that the cross-platform policy is therefore `DO use <details>/<summary>`. But the `severity-table` layout itself violates that policy by using `<details>` only for summaries >500 chars while the other 19 layouts never use it. Either the rule should say "DO use <details> only when the summary is verbose" with a documented threshold (the `VERBOSE_THRESHOLD_CHARS = 500` constant inside `layoutSeverityTable`), or the cross-platform claim is inaccurate — pick one and align the prose with the implementation.

`medium` `maintainability`

`VERBOSE_THRESHOLD_CHARS = 500` is a magic number embedded deep inside `layoutSeverityTable`. Promote it to a module-level `const SEVERITY_TABLE_VERBOSE_THRESHOLD_CHARS = 500` near the other constants (or fold it into the `LayoutId` config map). Today the threshold is invisible to other layouts that might want consistent collapsibility behavior.

`low` `maintainability`

`redact()` silently does nothing when `secrets` is empty, but it also silently does nothing when a secret is the empty string (early-continues). Document this behavior — an empty-string secret is meaningless but worth surfacing in a comment so future readers don't worry about a silent no-op. (Minor; not blocking.)

`medium` `correctness`

`layoutSeverityTable` calls `c.category` inside the `cell()` call without checking that `category` is a defined field on `LiveReviewComment`. If a caller passes a comment without `category` (which the existing test fixtures do for some shapes — see `preview-parent-card.test.ts` fixtures like `{ path, line, body, severity, category }` — every fixture DOES set category, but `LiveReviewComment` types should be checked). The runtime will print `undefined` in the cell. Add a `?? "general"` fallback like `layoutChecklist` does for category-or-general grouping.

`low` `maintainability`

In `layoutReleaseNotes`, the index objects `buckets["🔴 Fixes (high/critical)"]!` use non-null assertions. If a future contributor removes a bucket key from the `buckets` literal, the `!` will silently mask a runtime `undefined.push(...)` crash. Either build the bucket array via `SEVERITY_RANK_TO_BUCKET` mapping (no non-null) or split the lookup into a constant map.

`medium` `correctness`

`ReviewData` requires `postedComments: readonly LiveReviewComment[]`. Several callers in existing production code (`run.ts`, `live-merge.ts`, fixture builders in tests) construct inputs that omit `postedComments` and rely on the legacy fallback inside `buildReviewBody`. The `buildReviewBody` in `live-shared.ts` performs the `input.postedComments ?? input.review.comments` fallback before dispatch — but every direct caller of `renderSummary(layout, data)` outside `buildReviewBody` will now type-error or render with an empty table. Document this contract clearly and add at least one runtime assertion (`if (!data.postedComments) throw …`) so misuses fail loud, not silent.

`low` `maintainability`

`export const countBySeverity = countBySeverityUtil` was kept for backward compatibility, but the doc comment claims "external callers (`preparePostedReview`, the live tests) import this helper from `live-shared.ts`". `grep -r "from .*live-shared" src test` should be run before merging — if nothing actually imports it, the re-export should be deleted (otherwise it's dead surface area that the next refactor has to keep alive).

`low` `maintainability`

`SEVERITY_ORDER` is no longer imported here (it was deleted from the import list) but the new `summary-layouts.ts` re-exports nothing from `live-shared.ts` — the only consumers of `SEVERITY_ORDER` after this change are the renderer layouts. Confirms the import was removed only because the inline counts line is gone. Worth a one-line `// SEVERITY_ORDER moved to src/render/summary-layouts.ts via src/util/severity.ts` breadcrumb for the next reader.

`medium` `correctness`

`buildReviewBody` now silently fakes parity by always selecting the `"severity-table"` layout. There is no test or runtime guard preventing a caller from bypassing this and calling `renderSummary("dashboard", …)` — that would produce a card with a totally different shape (no `<details>`, no manifest last, etc.) that would still pass most assertions. Consider making `renderSummary` reject the call when called outside `buildReviewBody` for a "production" marker, or rename to underscore-prefix to mark it as internal-only.

`low` `maintainability`

`events.push([])` always pushes a new array even when the current event is `[]` after the final blank line. With `const events: string[][] = [[]]` plus `if (events[events.length - 1]!.length > 0)`, the trailing empty group is filtered out — but the logic depends on that `!` non-null assertion. If a contributor changes the lazy-init to `[]`, they'll hit a TypeError. Consider `events.length > 0 && events[events.length - 1]!.length > 0` and initialize lazily.

`medium` `correctness`

SSE reassembly concatenates `data:` lines with `
` per spec, but if the original encoded payload had a JSON-escaped `
` (which is what motivated this whole fix), the resulting `payload` will contain BOTH literal newlines (from re-assembly) and `
` escape sequences (from the original encoded value) when `extractTextPayload` calls `JSON.parse` on each per-event payload. This works today because `tryParseJson` decodes JSON-encoded `data:` frames, but it's worth a comment in `tryExtractSse` flagging that downstream `parseReviewPayload` needs `extractFirstBalancedObject`'s control-char escape — without it, big multi-fragment reviews would still fail. Currently the chain `tryExtractSse → extractFirstBalancedObject → parseReviewPayload` does work, but it's fragile. Document the invariant.

`high` `security`

`process.stderr.write(...JSON.stringify(textPayload.slice(0, 200)))` may leak secrets to stderr in non-debug modes if `secrets: []` redaction is not applied first. The current implementation only triggers when `UMACTUALLY_DEBUG_RAW === "1"`, but if the env var is set by a curious user or by a security scanner, the raw response (which can contain a hardcoded secret in the provider's review) writes to a shared CI log. Apply `redactSecrets(textPayload, secretSet)` before `JSON.stringify` in both branches.

`high` `security`

The `[DEBUG-RAW]` stderr writes do not include a secret-detection pass on `textPayload` before logging first/last 200 chars. Even though secrets are redacted in the diff before model submission, the provider may ECHO secret-pattern strings in its review (e.g. the model quotes the secret it just saw to explain its concern). Apply the redaction list before serializing.

`medium` `correctness`

`process.env["UMACTUALLY_DEBUG_RAW"] = "1"` mutates a process-global from a CLI command dispatcher. If `runOrchestrator` runs multiple reviews in the same process (e.g. a concurrent batch), the flag leaks across reviews and bleeds debug output into later runs' logs. Either use a per-call context object or unset the env after the call.

`medium` `correctness`

`needsRebuild()` compares mtime only on the source-vs-output pair of `src/cli/live-shared.ts → .layout-viewer-build/cli/live-shared.js`. But `live-shared.ts` now imports from `src/render/summary-layouts.ts`, which also needs recompilation when its source changes. Either rebuild unconditionally, or scan all `.ts` imports and rebuild if any source mtime > output. Today the script silently serves stale output.

`medium` `correctness`

`statMtime()` uses `readFileSync(p).atimeMs` (access time) instead of `mtimeMs` (modification time). This is incorrect for staleness checks — files with no recent access but updated content will read `atimeMs = old`. Replace with `statSync(p).mtimeMs`.

`low` `maintainability`

`buildHtml()` trims `samples.busy()` for the baseline rendering — but if a caller passes `--samples=clean,parse-failed` (no busy), the baseline comparison panel still calls `sampleBusy()`, which is harmless but produces output unrelated to the filtered samples shown. Either error out or label the baseline block as "busy-only (independent sample)".

`low` `security`

Static file server is bound to `127.0.0.1` (good — no network exposure) but does NOT set `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, or CSP. Even for local-only QA, a rendered MD file with raw `<script>` could surprise a future contributor opening it via `file://`. Add at minimum `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.

`critical` `correctness`

The compiled `dist/cli.js` (and `dist/index.js`) contain the literal expression `const LAYOUTS = (/* unused pure expression or super */ null && ([ ... 20 entries ... ]))` — clearly a bundling artifact left over from an earlier syntax probe. TypeScript compiled `null && ([ ... ])` as `null && (…)` and the boolean short-circuits to `null`, so `LAYOUTS` is effectively undefined in the dist bundle while source `LAYOUTS` in `src/render/summary-layouts.ts` is the real `readonly LayoutId[]` array. This means `dist/*` consumers calling `renderSummary` will get a different result from `src/*` consumers. Rebuild the bundles (delete the probe code from source if it's still there) or pin the dist output explicitly.

`medium` `correctness`

Inside the `manifest()` function body in `dist/*`, the doc comment header references `<!-- umalready-pr-review:manifest {…} -->` (typo `umalready`). The actual emitted HTML comment in the source uses `<!-- umactually-pr-review:manifest`. Downstream tooling that greps the dist for the marker will fail to find `umactually-pr-review:manifest` references documented under the wrong spelling. Rebuild the dist from current source.

`low` `correctness`

Adding `.layout-viewer-build/` to `.gitignore` is correct, but the new `scripts/render-evidence.mjs` writes artifacts to `artifacts/manual/severity-table-*.md` — that path is already covered by the existing `artifacts/manual/` rule, good. Confirm that the dir is created (mkdirSync recursive) before the first write in both scripts so the gitignore-tracked path doesn't accidentally get committed.

`medium` `correctness`

`debug-raw-response: 'true'` is added to the workflow with a useful comment, but the action input may need to be wired into the action's `inputs:` block in `action.yml` (no diff for that file shown — confirm `action.yml` also defines `debug-raw-response` with `default: 'false'` and passes it through).

`medium` `correctness`

CLARITY-2 test has been rewritten to assert that the severity tally is somewhere between verdict and footer (no longer within 200 chars). This drops a strong guarantee — a reader scanning the parent card could legitimately complain that the table now pushes the tally below the fold. Consider keeping BOTH guarantees: tally within the body AND not occluded by anything collapsible (now trivially satisfied). The current test guarantees too little.

`high` `correctness`

CLARITY-4 test now asserts that the summary is NOT inside `<details>`. The doc-comment in `summary-layouts.ts` line 22 explicitly says `The severity-table layout uses <details> for verbose summaries (>500 chars)`. So the layout DOES use `<details>` for verbose summaries — this test would fail when invoked on the fixture `makeVerboseData()` from `summary-layouts.test.ts`. Either the test must `expect(body).not.toContain('<details>')` only for the SMALL summary case, or the new layout shouldn't use `<details>` at all. Pick one and stay consistent.

`low` `style`

Final file does not have a trailing newline. POSIX & most editors prefer files to end with newline; add one to avoid editor complaints and tools that strip trailing blank lines.

`low` `maintainability`

S5b verbose-summary test only checks `severity-table`. The doc claim in `summary-layouts.ts` line 22 says ALL layouts obey the same GFM rules, but only severity-table uses `<details>`. Either explicitly state that the `<details>`-wrap policy applies ONLY to severity-table, or extend the test to assert that all 20 layouts do NOT use `<details>` for short summaries (already covered by S5a) AND that the severity-table wraps verbose summaries (covered) — the test as written is fine; the doc comment is just underspecified.

`low` `correctness`

Severity-sort test uses fixtures that don't include `category` on some comments and the `layoutSeverityTable` invocation will pass `undefined` through `cell()`. Test should explicitly set `category` on every comment to avoid relying on `undefined` printing behavior of `String(undefined)` = `'undefined'`.

`low` `maintainability`

End-to-end test uses a raw `stream` variable with the SSE message hard-coded inside a single string. Real SSE streams come over the wire as multi-byte UTF-8, and vitest will load this file with whatever encoding is in .gitattributes. Add a comment noting that test fixtures assume UTF-8 source — if the repo ever switches to UTF-16, the literal `\n` in the `data:` payload would corrupt.

`low` `style`

File ends without newline (per leading diff context showing `\ No newline at end of file`). Add a trailing newline for consistency with the rest of the codebase.

`low` `maintainability`

Top-level docstring references `src/util/severity.ts` indirectly via `import SEVERITY_ORDER`. The intent comment in `summary-layouts.ts` claims cross-platform rules are verified on 2026-07-05 — a future date. Either rewrite as `verified in CI on PR #43` (with a real PR link) or remove the verification date so it doesn't read like a future-dated claim.
